sentences.zh: 吳允誠，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Wu Yuncheng was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuncheng was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 名把都帖木兒，居甘肅塞外塔溝地，官至平章。

translations.literal: His name was Badutiemuer; he lived at Tagou beyond the Gansu frontier and rose to the rank of pingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His name was Badutiemuer; he lived at Tagou beyond the Gansu frontier and had risen to the rank of pingzhang.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，與其黨倫都兒灰率妻子及部落五千、馬駝萬六千，因宋晟來歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle, he and his associate Lunduerhui led their wives and children, five thousand tribesmen, and sixteen thousand horses and camels to submit through Song Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle, he and his follower Lunduerhui brought their families, five thousand tribesmen, and sixteen thousand horses and camels to surrender, coming in through Song Cheng.

sentences.zh: 帝以蒙古人多同名，當賜姓別之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that many Mongols bore the same names and that surnames should be granted to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that many Mongols shared the same names and ordered that surnames be granted to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉俊請如洪武故事，編為勘合。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Jun requested that, following the Hongwu precedent, they be entered in registers of tally-verification.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Jun asked that, following the Hongwu precedent, they be registered on tally-verification rolls.

sentences.zh: 允誠得賜姓名，授右軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: Yuncheng received a granted surname and personal name and was appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng was granted a surname and personal name and appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 倫都兒灰亦賜姓名柴秉誠，授後軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: Lunduerhui likewise received the granted name Chai Bingcheng and was appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lunduerhui was likewise granted the name Chai Bingcheng and appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 余授官賜冠帶，給畜產鈔幣有差。

translations.literal: The remainder were given offices, granted caps and belts, and provided livestock and paper money in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were given offices, caps and belts, and livestock and paper money in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 使領所部居涼州耕牧。

translations.literal: They were made to lead their followers to settle at Liangzhou for farming and herding.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered to lead their followers to live at Liangzhou and farm and herd there.

sentences.zh: 晟以招徠功，封西寧侯。

translations.literal: Song Cheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining for his achievement in winning them over.
translations.idiomatic: Song Cheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining for his success in winning them over.

sentences.zh: 自是降附者益眾，邊境日安，由允誠始。

translations.literal: From this time those who surrendered and attached themselves grew ever more numerous, and the frontier daily grew secure—a trend that began with Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: From then on those who surrendered grew ever more numerous and the frontier grew daily more secure—a development that began with Yuncheng.

sentences.zh: 七年往亦集乃覘敵，擒哈剌等二十余人，進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he went to Yijinai to reconnoiter the enemy and captured Hala and more than twenty others, advancing to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went to Yijinai to scout the enemy, captured Hala and more than twenty others, and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年從出塞，敗本雅失裏，進右都督。

translations.literal: The next year he followed on a campaign beyond the frontier, defeated Benyashili, and was promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the right.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed a campaign beyond the frontier, defeated Benyashili, and was promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 尋進左都督。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 與中官王安追闊脫赤，至把力河獲之。

translations.literal: Together with the eunuch Wang An he pursued Kuotuochi and captured him at the Bali River.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the eunuch Wang An he pursued Kuotuochi and captured him at the Bali River.

sentences.zh: 封恭順伯，食祿千二百石，予世券。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Gongshun with an emolument of 1,200 piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Gongshun with an emolument of 1,200 piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 允誠三子：答蘭、管者、克勤。

translations.literal: Yuncheng had three sons: Dalans, Guanzhe, and Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng had three sons: Dalans, Guanzhe, and Keqin.

sentences.zh: 允誠與二子從軍，留其妻及管者居涼州。

translations.literal: Yuncheng and two sons went on campaign; his wife and Guanzhe remained at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng and two sons went on campaign, while his wife and Guanzhe remained at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 番人虎保等誘脅允誠眾，欲叛去。

translations.literal: A tribesman named Hubao and others enticed and coerced Yuncheng's followers, intending to rebel and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesman Hubao and others enticed and pressured Yuncheng's followers, planning to rebel and flee.

sentences.zh: 允誠妻與管者謀，召部將都指揮保住、卜顏不花等擒其黨，誅之。

translations.literal: Yuncheng's wife and Guanzhe plotted together and summoned the commanders Baozhu and Buyanbuhua to seize the conspirators and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng's wife and Guanzhe plotted together and summoned the commanders Baozhu and Buyanbuhua to seize the conspirators and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，降敕獎之，賜縑鈔羊米甚厚，授管者指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, sent down an edict of commendation, and granted silk, paper money, sheep, and grain in great abundance; Guanzhe was appointed assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, sent down a commendatory edict, and granted silk, paper money, sheep, and grain in great abundance; Guanzhe was appointed assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 保住賜姓名楊效誠，授指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Baozhu was granted the surname Yang Xiaocheng and appointed assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhu was granted the surname Yang Xiaocheng and appointed assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 韃靼可汗鬼力赤遇弒，其下多潰。

translations.literal: The Tatar khan Guilichi was assassinated, and many of his followers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Tatar khan Guilichi was assassinated, and many of his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 答蘭與別立哥請出塞自效，有功。

translations.literal: Dalans and Bielige requested permission to go beyond the frontier to offer their service, and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Dalans and Bielige asked to go beyond the frontier to prove themselves and won merit.

sentences.zh: 別立哥者，秉誠子也。

translations.literal: Bielige was Bingcheng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Bielige was Bingcheng's son.

sentences.zh: 帝征瓦剌，允誠父子皆從。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against the Oirats, Yuncheng and his sons all followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against the Oirats, Yuncheng and his sons all followed.

sentences.zh: 師還，命仍居涼州備邊。

translations.literal: On the army's return, he was ordered to continue residing at Liangzhou to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was ordered to remain at Liangzhou to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 允誠卒，贈國公，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: Yuncheng died and was posthumously enfeoffed as a duke of the state with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng died and was posthumously enfeoffed as a state duke with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，克忠與其弟都督克勤子瑾為後拒。

translations.literal: At the Tumu crisis, Kezhong and his younger brother the commissioner Keqin, Keqin's son Jin, served as the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tumu crisis, Kezhong and his younger brother the commissioner Keqin, with Keqin's son Jin, served as the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 寇突至，驟戰不勝。

translations.literal: The bandits suddenly arrived; in the sudden engagement they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suddenly arrived; in the sudden clash they could not hold.

sentences.zh: 敵兵據山上，飛矢石如雨，官軍死傷略盡。

translations.literal: The enemy held the heights above them; arrows and stones rained down like a storm, and the government troops were nearly all killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the heights; arrows and stones fell like rain, and the government troops were nearly all killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 克忠下馬射，矢竭，猶殺數人，與克勤俱歿於陣。

translations.literal: Kezhong dismounted to shoot; when his arrows were spent he still killed several men, and he and Keqin both fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhong dismounted to shoot; when his arrows were gone he still killed several men, and he and Keqin both died on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈邠國公，謚忠勇。

translations.literal: Kezhong was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin with the posthumous title Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhong was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bin with the posthumous title Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 克勤贈遵化伯，謚僖敏。

translations.literal: Keqin was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Zunhua with the posthumous title Ximin.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Zunhua with the posthumous title Ximin.

sentences.zh: 瑾被執，逃歸，嗣侯。

translations.literal: Jin was captured but escaped and returned, inheriting the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was captured but escaped and returned, and inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 英宗嘗欲使瑾守甘肅，辭曰：「臣，外人，若用臣守邊，恐外裔輕中國。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong once wished to have Jin guard Gansu; he declined, saying, "Your subject is an outsider; if Your Majesty employs me to guard the frontier, I fear the foreign tribes will hold China lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong once wished to have Jin guard Gansu; he declined, saying, "I am an outsider; if Your Majesty uses me to guard the frontier, I fear the foreign tribes will look down on China."

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 曹欽反，瑾與從弟琮聞變，椎長安門上告。

translations.literal: When Cao Qin rebelled, Jin and his cousin Cong, hearing of the disturbance, hammered on the Chang'an Gate to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Qin rebelled, Jin and his cousin Cong, hearing of the disturbance, hammered on the Chang'an Gate to report it.

sentences.zh: 門閉，欽攻不得入，遂縱火。

translations.literal: The gate was shut; Qin could not break in, so he set fires.
translations.idiomatic: The gate was shut tight; Qin could not break in, so he set fires.

sentences.zh: 瑾將五六騎與欽力戰死。

translations.literal: Jin led five or six horsemen and fought Qin fiercely until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin led five or six horsemen and fought Qin fiercely until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈涼國公，謚忠壯，予世券。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 三傳至曾孫繼爵。

translations.literal: The title passed through three generations to a great-great-grandson who inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed through three generations to a great-great-grandson who inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗守備南京。

translations.literal: He once served as commandant in defense at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as commandant in defense at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 傳子汝胤孫惟英，與繼爵皆總督京營戎政。

translations.literal: His line continued through sons Ruyin and grandson Weiying; both Ruyin and the title-holder Jijue served in turn as grand coordinators of metropolitan camp military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued through son Ruyin and grandson Weiying; both Ruyin and the title-holder Jijue served in turn as grand coordinators of metropolitan camp military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，都城陷，汝胤弟勛衛汝征偕妻女投繯死。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, Ruyin's younger brother the guard officer Ruzheng hanged himself together with his wife and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, Ruyin's younger brother the guard officer Ruzheng hanged himself with his wife and daughters.

sentences.zh: 管者卒，子玘嗣。

translations.literal: When Guanzhe died, his son Qi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhe died, his son Qi inherited.

sentences.zh: 管者妻早奴亦有智略，嘗親入朝獻良馬。

translations.literal: Guanzhe's wife Zaonu was also resourceful; she once went in person to court to present fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhe's wife Zaonu was also shrewd; she once went to court in person to present fine horses.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多其忠。

translations.literal: The court greatly admired her loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The court greatly admired her loyalty.

sentences.zh: 玘卒，管者弟克勤子琮嗣，鎮守寧夏。

translations.literal: When Qi died, Guanzhe's younger brother Keqin's son Cong inherited and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi died, Guanzhe's younger brother Keqin's son Cong inherited and garrisoned Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，滿四反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, Man Si rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chenghua, Man Si rebelled.

sentences.zh: 琮坐激變，且臨陣先退，下獄論死。

translations.literal: Cong was convicted of having provoked the uprising and of having withdrawn first in battle; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was convicted of having provoked the uprising and of having retreated first in battle; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 謫戍邊，爵除。

translations.literal: He was banished to serve on the frontier, and the peerage was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to frontier service, and the peerage was abolished.

sentences.zh: 薛斌，蒙古人，本名脫歡。

translations.literal: Xue Bin was a Mongol; his original name was Tuohuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bin was a Mongol; his original name was Tuohuan.

sentences.zh: 父薛臺，洪武中歸附，賜姓薛，累官燕山右護衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His father Xuetai submitted in the Hongwu era, was granted the surname Xue, and rose through repeated appointments to assistant commander of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuetai submitted in the Hongwu era, was granted the surname Xue, and rose through repeated appointments to assistant commander of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 斌嗣職，從起兵，累遷都督僉事。

translations.literal: Bin inherited the post, joined the Prince of Yan in raising troops, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Bin inherited the post, joined the Prince of Yan in raising troops, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從北征有功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: He followed the northern campaigns with merit and was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the northern campaigns with merit and was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 永樂十八年封永順伯，祿九百石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yongle he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongshun with an emolument of 900 piculs; his heirs were to hold the rank of commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yongle he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongshun with an emolument of 900 piculs; his heirs were to hold the rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 斌卒，子壽童方五歲。

translations.literal: When Bin died, his son Shoutong was only five years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin died, his son Shoutong was only five years old.

sentences.zh: 從父貴引見仁宗，立命嗣伯，賜名綬。

translations.literal: His uncle Gui presented him to Emperor Renzong, who at once ordered him to inherit the earldom and bestowed the name Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Gui presented him to Emperor Renzong, who at once ordered him to inherit the earldom and bestowed the name Shou.

sentences.zh: 長，驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was fierce and valiant in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was fierce and valiant in battle.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年秋，與成國公朱勇等遇敵於鷂兒嶺。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong he met the enemy at Yao'erling together with the Duke of Cheng Zhu Yong and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong he met the enemy at Yao'erling together with the Duke of Cheng Zhu Yong and others.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，弦斷矢盡，猶持空弓擊敵。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; his bowstring snapped and his arrows were exhausted, yet he still struck the enemy with an empty bow.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated; his bowstring snapped and his arrows were spent, yet he still struck the enemy with an empty bow.

sentences.zh: 敵怒，支解之。

translations.literal: The enemy in anger dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy in anger dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 既而知其本蒙古人也，曰：「此吾同類，宜勇健若此。

translations.literal: When they later learned he was originally a Mongol, they said, "This man is one of us—he ought to be as brave and strong as this."
translations.idiomatic: When they later learned he was originally a Mongol, they said, "He is one of us—he ought to be as brave and strong as this."

sentences.zh: 」相與哭之。

translations.literal: They wept for him together.
translations.idiomatic: They wept for him together.

sentences.zh: 謚武毅。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 子輔，孫勛，並得嗣伯。

translations.literal: His sons Fu and grandson Xun both inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Fu and grandson Xun both inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 勛子璽乃嗣指揮使，如券文。

translations.literal: Xun's son Xi then inherited the commander's post, as the patent stipulated.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Xi then inherited the commander's post, as the patent stipulated.

sentences.zh: 子忠前死，忠子英嗣伯。

translations.literal: Bin's son Zhong had died earlier; Zhong's son Ying inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's son Zhong had died earlier; Zhong's son Ying inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 卒，子璽嗣。

translations.literal: When Ying died, his son Xi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, his son Xi inherited.

sentences.zh: 坐貪淫奪爵。

translations.literal: He was deprived of his rank for greed and licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was deprived of his rank for greed and licentiousness.

sentences.zh: 久乃復之。

translations.literal: Only after a long interval was the title restored.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was the title restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，從弟琮嗣。

translations.literal: He died without sons, and his younger cousin Cong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons, and his younger cousin Cong inherited.

sentences.zh: 四傳至玄孫遵周。

translations.literal: The title passed through four generations to a great-great-grandson Zunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed through four generations to a great-great-grandson Zunzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，京師陷，被殺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 滕定，父瓚住，元樞密知院。

translations.literal: Teng Ding's father Zanzhu was a Yuan privy council vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Ding's father Zanzhu was a Yuan privy council vice-director.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，來降。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he came over and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he came over and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 授會州衛指揮僉事，賜姓滕。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant commander of Huizhou Guard and granted the surname Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant commander of Huizhou Guard and granted the surname Teng.

sentences.zh: 從燕起兵，進燕山右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He joined the Prince of Yan in raising troops and was promoted commander of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Prince of Yan in raising troops and was promoted commander of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，定嗣官，屢從出塞，有功，進至都督僉事。

translations.literal: When he died, Ding inherited the post; he repeatedly followed campaigns beyond the frontier and, for his merit, rose to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Ding inherited the post; he repeatedly followed campaigns beyond the frontier and, for his merit, rose to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年封奉化伯，祿八百石。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he was enfeoffed as Earl of Fenghua with an emolument of 800 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuande he was enfeoffed as Earl of Fenghua with an emolument of 800 piculs.

sentences.zh: 正統初卒。

translations.literal: He died early in the Zhengtong reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 子福嗣，為指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Fu inherited and held the post of commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu inherited the post of commander.

sentences.zh: 金順，本名阿魯哥失裏。

translations.literal: Jin Shun; his original name was Alugeshili.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shun, whose original name was Alugeshili.

sentences.zh: 永樂中來降，授大寧都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era he came over and surrendered and was appointed assistant commander of the Daning Command.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle he surrendered and was appointed assistant commander of the Daning Command.

sentences.zh: 從敗本雅失裏，又敗阿魯臺，累進都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Benyashili and again defeated Aruqtai, rising through repeated promotions to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in defeating Benyashili and again defeating Aruqtai, and rose through repeated promotions to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年從巡北邊，有斬捕功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he followed the tour of the northern frontier and won merit in killing and capturing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he accompanied the tour of the northern frontier and won merit in killing and capturing enemies.

sentences.zh: 明年封順義伯，祿八百石。

translations.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shunyi with an emolument of 800 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shunyi with an emolument of 800 piculs.

sentences.zh: 卒，子忠嗣，為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Zhong inherited and served as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Zhong inherited and served as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 金忠者，蒙古王子也先土幹也。

translations.literal: Jin Zhong was a Mongol prince of the Yixian Tugan line.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhong was a Mongol prince of the Yixian Tugan line.

sentences.zh: 素桀黠，為阿魯臺所忌。

translations.literal: He had always been fierce and cunning and was resented by Aruqtai.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been fierce and cunning and was resented by Aruqtai.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十一年，成祖親征漠北，至上莊堡，率妻子部屬來降。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yongle, when the founding emperor campaigned in person in the northern desert and reached Shangzhuang Fort, Zhong led his wife, children, and followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yongle, when the founding emperor campaigned in person in the northern desert and reached Shangzhuang Fort, Zhong led his wife, children, and followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時六師深入，寇已遠遁。

translations.literal: At the time the six armies had penetrated deep, and the bandits had already fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the six armies had penetrated deep, and the enemy had already fled far away.

sentences.zh: 帝方恥無功，見其來歸，大喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was ashamed of achieving no success; when he saw Zhong come over, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ashamed of having achieved nothing; when he saw Zhong surrender, he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 賜姓名，封忠勇王，賜冠帶織金襲衣，命坐列侯下。

translations.literal: He granted him a surname and personal name, enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong, bestowed cap, belt, and brocade court robes, and ordered him to be seated below the ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him a surname and personal name, enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong, bestowed cap, belt, and brocade court robes, and ordered him seated below the ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 輟御前珍羞賜之，復賜金銀寶器。

translations.literal: He set aside delicacies from before the throne to grant him and again bestowed gold, silver, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside delicacies from the imperial table to grant him and again bestowed gold, silver, and precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 忠大喜過望。

translations.literal: Zhong was delighted beyond his hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was delighted beyond his hopes.

sentences.zh: 班師在道，忠騎從，數問寇中事，眷寵日隆。

translations.literal: On the return march he rode in attendance; the emperor repeatedly questioned him about affairs among the bandits, and his favor daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he rode in attendance; the emperor repeatedly questioned him about affairs among the enemy, and his favor grew daily.

sentences.zh: 明年，忠請為前鋒，討阿魯臺自效。

translations.literal: The next year Zhong requested to serve as vanguard and campaign against Aruqtai to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhong asked to serve as vanguard and campaign against Aruqtai to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 帝初不許。

translations.literal: At first the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 會大同、開平警報至，諸將請從忠言。

translations.literal: When alarms arrived from Datong and Kaiping, the generals asked to follow Zhong's advice.
translations.idiomatic: When alarms arrived from Datong and Kaiping, the generals asked to follow Zhong's advice.

sentences.zh: 帝復出塞，忠與陳懋為前鋒。

translations.literal: The emperor again went beyond the frontier; Zhong and Chen Mao served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again went beyond the frontier; Zhong and Chen Mao served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 而阿魯臺聞王師復出，倉皇渡答蘭納木兒河遁去。

translations.literal: But when Aruqtai heard the royal army was coming out again, he fled in panic across the Dalana Muir River.
translations.idiomatic: But when Aruqtai heard the royal army was coming out again, he fled in panic across the Dalana Muir River.

sentences.zh: 忠、懋至河不見寇，抵白邙山，卒無所遇，乃班師。

translations.literal: Zhong and Mao reached the river but found no bandits; they pressed on to Mount Baiwang and in the end encountered nothing, so they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Mao reached the river but found no enemy; they pressed on to Mount Baiwang and in the end encountered nothing, so they withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，加太子太保，並支二俸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong succeeded to the throne, Zhong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and drew two salaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded to the throne, Zhong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and drew two salaries.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年親征兀良哈，敗寇於寬河。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande the emperor campaigned in person against the Uriangqai and defeated the bandits at the Kuan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande the emperor campaigned in person against the Uriangqai and defeated the enemy at the Kuan River.

sentences.zh: 忠與把臺請自效，帝許之。

translations.literal: Zhong and Batui asked to prove themselves, and the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Batui asked to prove themselves, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 或言不可遣，帝曰：「去留任所欲耳。

translations.literal: Some said they should not be sent; the emperor said, "Whether they stay or go is for them to choose as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: Some said they should not be sent; the emperor said, "Whether they stay or go is for them to choose as they wish.

sentences.zh: 朕有天下，獨少此二人邪。

translations.literal: I possess the empire—am I short of these two men alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Do I lack these two men alone?"

sentences.zh: 」二人獲數十人、馬牛數百來獻。

translations.literal: The two men captured several dozen people and several hundred horses and cattle and came to present them.
translations.idiomatic: The two captured several dozen people and several hundred horses and cattle and came to present them.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，命中官酌以金卮，遂賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered a eunuch to pour wine from a golden goblet, then bestowed it on them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered a eunuch to pour wine from a golden goblet, then bestowed it on them.

sentences.zh: 明年加太保。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 六年秋卒。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 命有司治喪葬。

translations.literal: He was ordered to have the relevant offices arrange his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices were ordered to arrange his funeral.

sentences.zh: 把臺者，忠之甥，從忠來降，授都督僉事。

translations.literal: Batui was Zhong's nephew; he followed Zhong in surrendering and was appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Batui was Zhong's nephew; he followed Zhong in surrendering and was appointed assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，賜姓名蔣信。

translations.literal: In the early Xuande era he was granted the surname and personal name Jiang Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xuande era he was granted the surname and personal name Jiang Xin.

sentences.zh: 正統中，封忠勇伯。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era he was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era he was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 從駕陷土木，也先使隸賽罕王帳下。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial progress and was trapped at Tumu; Esen had him placed under the account of Prince Saihan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial progress and was trapped at Tumu; Esen had him placed under the account of Prince Saihan.

sentences.zh: 信雖居朔漠，誌常在中國。

translations.literal: Though Xin lived in the northern desert, his heart was always set on China.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xin lived in the northern desert, his heart was always set on China.

sentences.zh: 每詣上皇所慟哭，擁衛頗至。

translations.literal: He often went to the place where the former emperor was held and wept bitterly, and his protection was quite thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He often went to where the former emperor was held and wept bitterly, and his protection was quite thorough.

sentences.zh: 已，竟從駕還，詔復給其祿。

translations.literal: Later he at last followed the imperial progress back; an edict restored his emolument.
translations.idiomatic: Later he at last followed the imperial progress back; an edict restored his emolument.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingtai he died.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚僖順。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as a marquis with the posthumous title Xishun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as a marquis with the posthumous title Xishun.

sentences.zh: 子也兒索忽襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yiersuohu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiersuohu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 天順初，更名善。

translations.literal: In the early Tianshun era his name was changed to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianshun era his name was changed to Shan.

sentences.zh: 弘治中卒。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi era he died.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵絕。

translations.literal: He had no sons, and the peerage was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, and the peerage was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 李英，西番人。

translations.literal: Li Ying was a man of the Western Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying was a man of the Western Tribes.

sentences.zh: 父南哥，洪武中率眾歸附，授西寧州同知，累功進西寧衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His father Nange in the Hongwu era led his followers to submit and was appointed vice prefect of Xining Prefecture; through accumulated merit he rose to assistant commander of Xining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nange in the Hongwu era led his followers to submit and was appointed vice prefect of Xining Prefecture; through accumulated merit he rose to assistant commander of Xining Guard.

sentences.zh: 英嗣官。

translations.literal: Ying inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: Ying inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，番酋老的罕叛，英擊之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle the tribal chief Laodehan rebelled, and Ying attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongle the tribal chief Laodehan rebelled, and Ying attacked him.

sentences.zh: 討來川，俘斬三百六十人。

translations.literal: He campaigned in Laichuan and captured and beheaded 360 men.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Laichuan and captured and beheaded 360 men.

sentences.zh: 夜雪，賊遁，追盡獲之，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Snow fell at night; the bandits fled, and in pursuit he captured them all, advancing to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell at night; the bandits fled, and in pursuit he captured them all, advancing to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 番僧張答裏麻者，通譯書。

translations.literal: The Tibetan monk Zhang Dalima was skilled at translating books.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan monk Zhang Dalima was skilled at translating books.

sentences.zh: 成祖授以左覺義。

translations.literal: The founding emperor appointed him Left Awakener of the Faith.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor appointed him Left Awakener of the Faith.

sentences.zh: 居西寧，恣甚。

translations.literal: He lived at Xining and behaved with extreme license.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Xining and behaved with extreme license.

sentences.zh: 以計取西番貢使資，納逋逃，交通外域，肆惡十余年。

translations.literal: By stratagem he took the assets of Western Tribes tribute envoys, harbored fugitives, communicated with foreign regions, and committed outrages for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: By stratagem he took the assets of Western Tribes tribute envoys, harbored fugitives, communicated with foreign regions, and committed outrages for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 英發其事，磔死，籍其家。

translations.literal: Ying exposed the matter; he was dismembered and executed, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Ying exposed the matter; he was dismembered and executed, and his household was registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 西陲快之。

translations.literal: The western frontier rejoiced at this.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier rejoiced at this.

sentences.zh: 末年，中官喬來喜、鄧誠等使西域，道安定、曲先，遇賊見殺，掠所賫金幣。

translations.literal: In his later years the eunuchs Qiao Laixi and Deng Cheng and others were sent to the Western Regions; passing Anding and Quxian they met bandits who killed them and plundered the gold and coins they carried.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the eunuchs Qiao Laixi and Deng Cheng and others were sent to the Western Regions; passing Anding and Quxian they met bandits who killed them and plundered the gold and coins they carried.

sentences.zh: 仁宗璽書諭赤斤、罕東及安定、曲先，詰賊主名。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong sent sealed edicts to Chijin, Handong, and Anding and Quxian, demanding the names of the bandit leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong sent sealed edicts to Chijin, Handong, and Anding and Quxian, demanding the names of the bandit leaders.

sentences.zh: 而敕英與土官指揮康壽等進討。

translations.literal: He also ordered Ying and the native-official commander Kang Shou and others to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Ying and the native-official commander Kang Shou and others to advance and attack.

sentences.zh: 英诇知安定指揮哈三孫散哥、曲先指揮散即思實殺使者，遂率兵西入。

translations.literal: Ying learned through reconnaissance that Anding commander Hasan's grandson Sange and Quxian commander Sanjisi had in fact killed the envoys, and he led his troops west.
translations.idiomatic: Ying learned through reconnaissance that Anding commander Hasan's grandson Sange and Quxian commander Sanjisi had in fact killed the envoys, and he led his troops west.

sentences.zh: 賊驚走。

translations.literal: The bandits fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 追擊，逾昆侖山，深入數百里。

translations.literal: He pursued them beyond Mount Kunlun, penetrating several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them beyond Mount Kunlun, penetrating several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 至雅令闊，與安定賊遇，大敗之，俘斬千一百余人，獲馬牛雜畜十四萬。

translations.literal: At Yaling Kuo he met the Anding bandits and defeated them greatly, capturing and beheading more than 1,100 men and taking 140,000 mixed livestock of horses and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: At Yaling Kuo he met the Anding bandits and defeated them greatly, capturing and beheading more than 1,100 men and taking 140,000 mixed livestock of horses and cattle.

sentences.zh: 曲先賊聞風遠遁，安定王桑爾加失夾等懼，詣闕謝罪。

translations.literal: The Quxian bandits, hearing the news, fled far away; the king of Anding Sang'erjiashi and others were afraid and came to the court to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The Quxian bandits, hearing the news, fled far away; the king of Anding Sang'erjiashi and others were afraid and came to the court to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉英功，遣使褒諭，宴勞之，令馳驛入朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong praised Ying's achievement, sent envoys to commend him, feasted and rewarded him, and ordered him to enter court by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong praised Ying's achievement, sent envoys to commend him, feasted and rewarded him, and ordered him to enter court by relay post.

sentences.zh: 既至，擢右府左都督，賜賚加等。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was promoted to left commissioner of the Right Military Commission and granted rewards of a higher grade.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he was promoted to left commissioner of the Right Military Commission and granted rewards of a higher grade.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年封會寧伯，祿千一百石，並封南哥如子爵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huining with an emolument of 1,100 piculs, and Nange was also enfeoffed like a viscount's son.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huining with an emolument of 1,100 piculs, and Nange was also enfeoffed like a viscount's son.

sentences.zh: 英恃功而驕，所為多不法。

translations.literal: Ying relied on his achievements and became arrogant; his conduct was often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Ying relied on his achievements and became arrogant; his conduct was often unlawful.

sentences.zh: 寧夏總兵官史昭奏英父子有異志。

translations.literal: The regional commander of Ningxia Shi Zhao memorialized that Ying and his father harbored disloyal intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander of Ningxia Shi Zhao memorialized that Ying and his father harbored disloyal intentions.

sentences.zh: 南哥上章辯。

translations.literal: Nange submitted a memorial in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Nange submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 賜敕慰諭之。

translations.literal: An edict of comfort and reassurance was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of comfort and reassurance was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 英家西寧，招逋逃七百余戶，置莊墾田，豪奪人產，復為兵部及言官所劾。

translations.literal: Ying's household was at Xining; he recruited more than 700 fugitive households, established estates and opened farmland, and seized others' property by force; he was again impeached by the Ministry of War and censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's household was at Xining; he recruited more than 700 fugitive households, established estates and opened farmland, and seized others' property by force; he was again impeached by the Ministry of War and censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 帝宥英，追逃者入官。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Ying and had the fugitives entered into official registers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Ying and had the fugitives entered into official registers.

sentences.zh: 七年，西寧指揮祁震子成當襲父職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Qi Zhen's son Cheng was due to inherit his father's post as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Qi Zhen's son Cheng was due to inherit his father's post as commander.

sentences.zh: 庶兄監藏，英甥也，欲奪之。

translations.literal: The son by a concubine Jiancang, who was also Ying's nephew, wished to seize it from him.
translations.idiomatic: The son by a concubine Jiancang, who was also Ying's nephew, wished to seize it from him.

sentences.zh: 成從祖太平攜成赴京辯。

translations.literal: Cheng's great-uncle Taiping took Cheng to the capital to argue the case.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's great-uncle Taiping took Cheng to the capital to argue the case.

sentences.zh: 英遣人篡取太平及其義兒杖之，義兒竟死。

translations.literal: Ying sent men to seize Taiping and his adopted son and beat them; the adopted son died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent men to seize Taiping and his adopted son and beat them; the adopted son died in the end.

sentences.zh: 言官交劾，並及前罪，遂下英詔獄，奪爵論死。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached him in succession, including his earlier crimes; Ying was thereupon imprisoned by imperial edict, deprived of his rank, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached him in succession, including his earlier crimes; Ying was thereupon imprisoned by imperial edict, deprived of his rank, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 正統二年始釋。

translations.literal: Only in the second year of Zhengtong was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the second year of Zhengtong was he released.

sentences.zh: 後稍給其祿。

translations.literal: Later his emolument was gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his emolument was gradually restored.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，官其子錦衣指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, he appointed Ying's son Chang as vice commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, he appointed Ying's son Chang as vice commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋進都指揮使，用薦擢左軍都督僉事，屢分典營務，以嚴慎稱。

translations.literal: He was soon advanced to commander and, on recommendation, promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Left Army, repeatedly overseeing camp affairs and known for strict caution.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon advanced to commander and, on recommendation, promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief of the Left Army, repeatedly overseeing camp affairs and known for strict caution.

sentences.zh: 英從子文，宣德間為陜西行都司都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Ying's nephew Wen in the Xuande era served as assistant commander of the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's nephew Wen in the Xuande era served as assistant commander of the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 西番思俄可嘗盜他部善馬，都指揮穆肅求不得。

translations.literal: The Western Tribes chieftain Si'eke once stole fine horses from another tribe; the commander Mu Su could not recover them.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Tribes chieftain Si'eke once stole fine horses from another tribe; the commander Mu Su could not recover them.

sentences.zh: 會思俄可以畜產鬻於邊，肅誣以盜，收掠致死，番人惶駭思亂。

translations.literal: When Si'eke came to sell livestock at the frontier, Su falsely charged him with theft, seized and plundered him until he died; the tribesmen were terrified and thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Si'eke came to sell livestock at the frontier, Su falsely charged him with theft, seized and plundered him until he died; the tribesmen were terrified and thought of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 文劾之，逮肅下吏，西陲以寧。

translations.literal: Wen impeached him; Su was arrested and sent to the law officers, and the western frontier was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wen impeached him; Su was arrested and sent to the law officers, and the western frontier was thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 累官都指揮使。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated appointments to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated appointments to commander.

sentences.zh: 天順元年冒迎駕功，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he falsely claimed merit in welcoming the imperial progress and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun he falsely claimed merit in welcoming the imperial progress and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以右都督出鎮大同。

translations.literal: Before long, as commissioner-in-chief of the right he went out to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as commissioner-in-chief of the right he went out to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 寇二千余騎犯威遠，文率師敗之，封高陽伯。

translations.literal: When more than 2,000 enemy horsemen invaded Weiyuan, Wen led his troops and defeated them and was enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When more than 2,000 enemy horsemen invaded Weiyuan, Wen led his troops and defeated them and was enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 石亨敗，革奪門冒功者官。

translations.literal: When Shi Heng was defeated, offices of those who had falsely claimed merit in the Gate Seizure were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng was defeated, offices of those who had falsely claimed merit in the Gate Seizure were stripped.

sentences.zh: 文自首，帝以守邊不問。

translations.literal: Wen confessed on his own; the emperor, because he was guarding the frontier, did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wen confessed on his own; the emperor, because he was guarding the frontier, did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，孛來大舉入寇，文按兵不戰。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, Bolai invaded on a large scale; Wen held his troops and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year, Bolai invaded on a large scale; Wen held his troops and did not fight.

sentences.zh: 遂入雁門，大掠忻、代諸州。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon entered Yanmen and plundered greatly in the prefectures of Xin and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits thereupon entered Yanmen and plundered greatly in the prefectures of Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 京師震恐。

translations.literal: The capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 寇退，征文下詔獄，論斬。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, Wen was summoned and imprisoned by imperial edict and sentenced to execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew, Wen was summoned and imprisoned by imperial edict and sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 帝宥文死，降都督僉事，立功延綏。

translations.literal: The emperor spared Wen from death, reduced him to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and ordered him to win merit on the Yan-Sui frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared Wen from death, reduced him to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and ordered him to win merit on the Yan-Sui frontier.

sentences.zh: 既而進都督同知。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 成化中，哈密為土魯番所並，求救於朝。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua era, Hami was annexed by Turfan and appealed to the court for help.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, Turfan annexed Hami, which appealed to the court for aid.

sentences.zh: 詔文與右通政劉文往甘肅經略之，無功而還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wen and the Vice Commissioner of the Right Liu Wen to go to Gansu to oversee the matter; they returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wen and Right Vice Commissioner Liu Wen to Gansu to manage the affair, but they returned without achieving anything.

sentences.zh: 弘治初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Hongzhi era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 正德初贈高陽伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was posthumously granted the title Earl of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 毛勝，字用欽，初名福壽，元右丞相伯卜花之孫。

translations.literal: Mao Sheng, styled Yongqin, originally named Fushou, was the grandson of the Yuan Right Chancellor Bobuhua.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Sheng, styled Yongqin, was originally named Fushou; he was the grandson of Bobuhua, right chancellor of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 伯父那海，洪武中歸附，以「靖難」功至都指揮同知，無子。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Naihai submitted to the dynasty in the Hongwu era and, for merit in the "Pacifying Difficulties" campaign, rose to vice commander-in-chief; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Naihai submitted during the Hongwu reign and, for service in the Pacifying the Realm campaign, reached vice commander-in-chief; he left no son.

sentences.zh: 勝父安太嗣為羽林指揮使，傳子濟，無子，勝嗣。

translations.literal: Sheng's father Antai inherited as commander of the Imperial Guard; it passed to his son Ji, who had no son, and Sheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's father Antai inherited the post of commander of the Imperial Guard; the line passed to Ji, who died without issue, and Sheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 論濟征北功，進都指揮使。

translations.literal: Assessing Ji's merit in the northern campaigns, he was advanced to commander.
translations.idiomatic: On account of Ji's northern campaign merit, he was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 嘗逃歸塞外，尋復自還。

translations.literal: He once fled back beyond the frontier and soon returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He once fled to the borderlands but soon came back of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 正統七年以征麓川功，擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong, for merit in the Luchuan campaign, he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 7, for his service against Luchuan, he was raised to assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 靖遠伯王驥請選在京番將舍人，捕苗雲南。

translations.literal: Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji requested that Mongolian officers and retainers in the capital be selected to suppress the Miao in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji asked that frontier officers and their retainers in the capital be chosen to hunt down the Miao rebels in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乃命勝與都督冉保統六百人往。

translations.literal: Sheng was thereupon ordered with Commissioner Ran Bao to lead six hundred men thither.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Commissioner Ran Bao were ordered to take six hundred men.

sentences.zh: 已，再征麓川，即命二人充左右參將。

translations.literal: Later, on the second Luchuan campaign, the two were at once appointed left and right deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Luchuan was campaigned against a second time, the two were immediately appointed left and right deputy generals.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進都督同知。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was advanced to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，也先謀入寇，勝偕平鄉伯陳懷等率京軍三萬鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year, Esen planned to invade; Sheng together with Pingxiang Earl Chen Huai and others led thirty thousand capital troops to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 14, as Esen planned an invasion, Sheng joined Pingxiang Earl Chen Huai and others in leading thirty thousand troops from the capital to hold Datong.

sentences.zh: 懷遇寇戰歿，勝脫還。

translations.literal: Huai met the bandits in battle and died; Sheng escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huai was killed in battle with the enemy; Sheng escaped and made it back.

sentences.zh: 以武清伯石亨薦，景帝進勝左都督，督三千營操練。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Wuqing Earl Shi Heng, Emperor Jing advanced Sheng to commissioner-in-chief of the left and put him in charge of drilling the Three Thousand Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Wuqing Earl Shi Heng, Emperor Jing promoted Sheng to left commissioner-in-chief and put him in charge of drilling the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗大擾，詔勝往討。

translations.literal: The Miao of Guizhou rose in great disturbance; an edict ordered Sheng to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao of Guizhou rose in great revolt, and Sheng was ordered to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 未行而也先逼京師。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Esen pressed upon the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Esen threatened the capital.

sentences.zh: 勝禦之彰義門北，擊退之。

translations.literal: Sheng met them north of the Zhangyi Gate and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng held them off north of Zhangyi Gate and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 越二日，引兵西直門外，解都督孫鏜圍。

translations.literal: Two days later he led troops outside the Xizhi Gate and relieved the siege of Commissioner Sun Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he marched outside Xizhi Gate and lifted Commissioner Sun Tang's siege.

sentences.zh: 明日，都督武興戰歿於彰義門，寇乘勝進。

translations.literal: The next day Commissioner Wu Xing died in battle at the Zhangyi Gate, and the bandits pressed forward on their victory.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Commissioner Wu Xing was killed at Zhangyi Gate, and the enemy pressed the advantage.

sentences.zh: 勝與都御史王竑急援之，寇遂引卻。

translations.literal: Sheng and the Censor-in-Chief Wang Ang rushed to their aid, and the bandits thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Censor-in-Chief Wang Ang hurried to reinforce them, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勝追襲至紫荊關，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Sheng pursued in attack to Zijing Pass with considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng pursued them to Zijing Pass and took a fair number of heads.

sentences.zh: 事定，乃命以左副總兵統河間、東昌降夷赴貴州。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was ordered as left deputy commander-in-chief to lead surrendered tribesmen of Hejian and Dongchang to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, he was ordered as left deputy commander-in-chief to lead surrendered tribesmen from Hejian and Dongchang to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 賊首韋同烈據香壚山作亂，勝與總兵梁缶、右副總兵方瑛等從總督王來分道夾擊。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Wei Tonglie occupied Xianglu Mountain and made rebellion; Sheng with Commander-in-Chief Liang Fou, right deputy commander Fang Ying, and others followed Governor Wang Lai in divided attacks from several routes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Wei Tonglie held Xianglu Mountain in revolt; Sheng joined Commander Liang Fou, right deputy commander Fang Ying, and others under Governor Wang Lai in a pincer attack along several routes.

sentences.zh: 勝進自重安江，大破之。

translations.literal: Sheng advanced from the Chong'an River and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng advanced from Chong'an River and routed them.

sentences.zh: 會師山下，環四面攻之。

translations.literal: The armies united below the mountain and attacked on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The armies converged at the foot of the mountain and attacked from all sides.

sentences.zh: 賊窘，縛同烈降。

translations.literal: The rebels were hard pressed and bound Tonglie to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, the rebels bound Tonglie and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還討湖廣巴馬諸處反賊，克二十余寨，擒賊首吳奉先等百四十人，斬首千余級，封南寧伯，予世券。

translations.literal: Returning, he campaigned against the rebels at Bama and elsewhere in Huguang, took more than twenty stockades, captured the rebel leaders Wu Fengxian and others (one hundred forty persons), and cut off more than a thousand heads; he was enfeoffed as Earl of Nanning and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned against rebels at Bama and elsewhere in Huguang, capturing over twenty stockades and 140 rebel leaders including Wu Fengxian, with more than a thousand enemy killed; he was enfeoffed Earl of Nanning and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 疏請更名，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting a name change, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to change his name, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 移鎮騰沖。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison at Tengchong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Tengchong.

sentences.zh: 金齒芒市長官刀放革潛結麓川遺孽思卜發為變，勝設策擒之。

translations.literal: The native official Dao Fangge of Mangshi in Jinchi secretly joined the Luchuan remnant Sibafa in rebellion; Sheng devised a stratagem and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchi's Mangshi native official Dao Fangge secretly colluded with Luchuan remnant Sibafa to rebel; Sheng laid a trap and captured him.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史牟俸劾其貪暴不法數十事，且言勝本降人，狡猾難制，今又數通外夷，恐貽邊患。

translations.literal: The touring censor Mou Feng impeached him on dozens of counts of greed, cruelty, and lawlessness, and moreover said Sheng was originally a surrendered tribesman, crafty and hard to control, and now repeatedly communicated with outer tribes, fearing he would cause frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Mou Feng impeached him on dozens of charges of corruption and brutality, adding that Sheng was originally a defector, cunning and hard to control, and was now repeatedly in contact with foreign tribes, a potential source of border trouble.

sentences.zh: 詔巡撫覆實，卒置不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grand coordinator to investigate the facts; in the end it was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the grand coordinator to verify the charges, but in the end no action was taken.

sentences.zh: 天順二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianshun year 2.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚莊毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis, with the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a marquis, with the posthumous title Zhuangyi (Steadfast and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子榮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 坐石亨黨，發廣西立功。

translations.literal: Implicated as a member of Shi Heng's faction, he was sent to Guangxi to win merit through service.
translations.idiomatic: Caught up in Shi Heng's faction, he was sent to Guangxi to earn merit in the field.

sentences.zh: 成化初，鎮貴州，尋移兩廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he garrisoned Guizhou, and soon was moved to the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he garrisoned Guizhou, then was transferred to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 卒，子文嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Wen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Wen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弘治初協守南京，傳爵至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he assisted in the defense of Nanjing; the peerage was transmitted until the fall of the Ming and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he helped defend Nanjing; the title passed down until the Ming fell, when the line died out.

sentences.zh: 焦禮，字尚節，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Jiao Li, styled Shangjie, was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Li, styled Shangjie, was of Mongol origin.

sentences.zh: 父把思臺，洪武中歸附，為通州衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His father Basitai submitted in the Hongwu era and served as assistant commander of the Tongzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Basitai submitted during Hongwu and served as assistant commander of the Tongzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 子勝嗣，傳至義榮，無子，以勝弟謙嗣，累功至都指揮同知。

translations.literal: His son Sheng succeeded; the line passed to Yirong, who had no son, and Sheng's younger brother Qian succeeded, rising through accumulated merit to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng inherited; the line continued to Yirong, who died without issue, and Sheng's younger brother Qian succeeded, rising through merit to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 卒，子管失奴幼，謙弟禮借襲其職，備禦遼東。

translations.literal: He died; his son Guanshinu was young, and Qian's younger brother Li borrowed the inheritance of the post and defended Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Guanshinu was still a child; Qian's younger brother Li held the post in his stead and defended Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，禮當還職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, Li ought to have returned the office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande, Li was due to return the post.

sentences.zh: 宣宗念禮守邊勞，命居職如故，別授管失奴指揮使。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor, mindful of Li's frontier labor, ordered him to remain in office as before and separately appointed Guanshinu commander.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Li's long service on the frontier, the Xuande Emperor let him keep the post and separately appointed Guanshinu as commander.

sentences.zh: 禮尋以年勞，累進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: Li soon, through years of service, rose in repeated steps to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li was soon promoted through seniority to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統中，積功至右都督。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era, through accumulated merit he reached commissioner-in-chief of the right.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong, accumulated merit raised him to right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，景帝命充左副總兵，守寧遠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, Emperor Jing appointed him left deputy commander-in-chief to guard Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was captured on campaign, Emperor Jing made him left deputy commander-in-chief to hold Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，也先逼京城，詔禮率師入衛。

translations.literal: Before long Esen pressed the capital; an edict ordered Li to lead troops in to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Esen threatened the capital, and Li was ordered to march in relief.

sentences.zh: 寇退還鎮。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew he returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，賊二千余騎犯興水堡，禮擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingtai, more than two thousand bandit horsemen invaded Xingshui Fort; Li struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 4, over two thousand enemy horsemen attacked Xingshui Fort; Li repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎勵，進左都督。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended and rewarded him, and he was advanced to commissioner-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a commendatory letter and promoted him to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，以禮守邊有功，召入覲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, because Li had merit in guarding the frontier he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Li was summoned to court for his frontier service.

sentences.zh: 封東寧伯，世襲，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Dongning, with hereditary succession, and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Earl of Dongning with hereditary succession and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 遣還鎮。

translations.literal: He was sent back to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 兵部以禮年垂八十，不可獨任，奏遣都指揮鄧鐸協同守備。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War, because Li was nearly eighty and could not bear sole responsibility, memorialized dispatching Commander Deng Duo to assist jointly in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War, citing Li's age of nearly eighty, recommended Commander Deng Duo to share the defense with him.

sentences.zh: 居無何，禮奏鐸欺侮，請更調。

translations.literal: Before long, Li memorialized that Duo insulted him and requested a transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li complained that Duo had mistreated him and asked for a replacement.

sentences.zh: 命都指揮張俊代鐸。

translations.literal: Commander Zhang Jun was ordered to replace Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhang Jun was appointed in Duo's place.

sentences.zh: 天順七年卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun he died at his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post in Tianshun year 7.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis, with the posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a marquis, with the posthumous title Xiangyi (Supporting and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 禮有膽略，精騎射，善以少擊眾。

translations.literal: Li had courage and stratagem, excelled in mounted archery, and was skilled at striking the many with the few.
translations.idiomatic: Li was bold and resourceful, a master of mounted archery, adept at defeating larger forces with smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 守寧遠三十余年，士卒樂為用，邊陲寧謐。

translations.literal: He guarded Ningyuan for more than thirty years; troops were glad to serve him, and the frontier was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years he held Ningyuan; his men served him willingly and the border stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 孫壽嗣爵。

translations.literal: His grandson Shou succeeded to the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，弟俊嗣。

translations.literal: He died without a son, and his younger brother Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died without issue, and his younger brother Jun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 成化末，歷鎮甘肅、寧夏。

translations.literal: At the end of Chenghua he successively garrisoned Gansu and Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Chenghua reign he held commands in Gansu and Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，掌南京前府，兼督操江。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era he oversaw the Nanjing Front Guard and concurrently supervised the Yangtze training fleet.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he directed the Nanjing Front Guard and supervised the Yangtze naval training.

sentences.zh: 出鎮貴州、湖廣。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison Guizhou and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He took field commands in Guizhou and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 俊少事商販，既貴，能下士，而折沖非所長。

translations.literal: Jun in youth worked as a merchant; once elevated, he could humbly treat scholars, yet breaking enemy momentum was not his forte.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had been a merchant in his youth; after rising in rank he treated men of talent with deference, but military command was not his strength.

sentences.zh: 卒，子淇嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Qi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘗分典京營。

translations.literal: He once shared in overseeing the capital camps.
translations.idiomatic: He served in rotation overseeing the capital armies.

sentences.zh: 正德中，賄劉瑾，出鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era he bribed Liu Jin and went out to garrison the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengde he bribed Liu Jin and was posted to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，弟洵嗣。

translations.literal: After a year he died, and his younger brother Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died within a year, and his younger brother Xun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 洵雖嗣爵，先業盡為淇妻所有。

translations.literal: Although Xun succeeded to the peerage, the family's earlier property was entirely possessed by Qi's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xun inherited the title, the family fortune had all passed to Qi's wife.

sentences.zh: 生母卒，無以葬，哀憤得疾卒。

translations.literal: His birth mother died, and he had no means to bury her; in grief and anger he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his biological mother died he could not afford a funeral; grief and anger brought on an illness that killed him.

sentences.zh: 無子，以再從子棟嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son, and his grand-nephew Dong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died without issue, and his grand-nephew Dong inherited.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，提督五軍營，兼掌中府。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era he supervised the Five Army Camps and concurrently directed the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing he directed the Five Army Camps and concurrently headed the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 逾十年，改總兵湖廣。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, he was changed to commander in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade he was transferred to overall command in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚莊僖。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhuangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhuangxi.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: The peerage was transmitted until the fall of the Ming and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed down until the fall of the dynasty, when the line died out.

sentences.zh: 毛忠，字允誠，初名哈喇，西陲人。

translations.literal: Mao Zhong, styled Yuncheng, originally named Hala, was a man of the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhong, styled Yuncheng, was originally named Hala; he came from the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 曾祖哈喇歹，洪武初歸附，起行伍為千戶，戰歿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Haladai submitted at the beginning of Hongwu, rose from the ranks to chiliarch, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Haladai submitted early in Hongwu, rose from the ranks to chiliarch, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 祖拜都從征哈密，亦戰歿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Baidu followed the campaign to Hami and likewise died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Baidu campaigned to Hami and also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 父寶以驍勇充總旗，至永昌百戶。

translations.literal: His father Bao, for fierce bravery, served as chief bannerman and rose to centurion of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao, renowned for valor, served as chief bannerman and rose to centurion at Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 忠襲職時，年二十。

translations.literal: When Zhong inherited the post, he was twenty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was twenty when he inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 膂力絕人，善騎射。

translations.literal: His bodily strength was matchless among men, and he excelled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed extraordinary strength and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 常從太宗北征。

translations.literal: He often followed the Taizong Emperor on northern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He often accompanied the Yongle Emperor on northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年征曲先叛寇，有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande he campaigned against the Qusian rebel bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 he campaigned against the Qusian rebels with distinction.

sentences.zh: 八年征亦不剌山，擒偽少師知院。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he campaigned at Yibulashan and captured the false Junior Preceptor and Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he campaigned at Mount Yibula and captured a pretender styled Junior Preceptor and Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年出脫歡山，十年征黑山寇，皆擒其酋。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out to Tuohuan Mountain, and in the tenth year campaigned against the Heishan bandits; in each case he captured their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he campaigned at Tuohuan Mountain, and in year 10 against the Heishan bandits, capturing their chiefs each time.

sentences.zh: 各進一官，歷指揮同知。

translations.literal: For each he was advanced one rank, until he held the office of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Each victory earned him a promotion until he reached vice commander.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，從都督蔣貴征朵兒只伯，先登陷陣，大獲，擢都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong he followed Commissioner Jiang Gui against Dorjiba, was first to ascend and break the line, gained greatly, and was promoted to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 3 he followed Commissioner Jiang Gui against Dorjiba, led the charge, won a major victory, and was promoted to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 十年以守邊勞，進同知，始賜姓。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for frontier-guarding labor, he was advanced to vice commander and first granted the surname Mao.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, for frontier service, he was made vice commander and first given the surname Mao.

sentences.zh: 明年，從總兵官任禮收捕沙洲衛都督喃哥部落，徙之塞內，進都指揮使。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Commander-in-Chief Ren Li in rounding up the tribes of the Shazhou Guard Commissioner Nange and relocating them within the frontier, and was advanced to commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Commander Ren Li in subduing the Shazhou Guard commissioner Nange's tribes and resettling them inside the border, and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年率師至罕東，生縶喃哥弟偽祁王鎖南奔並其部眾，擢都督僉事，始賜名忠。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led troops to Handong, captured alive Nange's younger brother the false Prince of Qi Suonanben and his following, and was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief; he was first granted the name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he marched to Handong, captured alive Nange's brother, the false Prince of Qi Suonanben, along with his followers, was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, and first received the name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 尋充右參將，協守甘肅。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed right deputy general to assist in guarding Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right deputy general to help defend Gansu.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，侍郎李實使漠北，還言忠數遣使通瓦剌。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, Vice Minister Li Shi was envoy to the northern deserts; on return he reported that Zhong had repeatedly sent envoys to communicate with the Oirat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai, Vice Minister Li Shi went on mission to the northern steppe and, upon return, reported that Zhong had repeatedly sent envoys to the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 詔執赴京。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that he be seized and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his arrest and escort to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，兵部論其罪，請置大辟。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, the Board of War assessed his offense and requested the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: After he arrived, the Board of War judged his offense and asked that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 景帝不許。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 請貶官，發福建立功。

translations.literal: They requested that he be demoted and sent to Fujian to earn merit through service.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that he be demoted and sent to Fujian to redeem himself by military achievement.

sentences.zh: 乃遣之福建，而官秩如故。

translations.literal: He was then dispatched to Fujian, while his official rank remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Fujian, but his rank was left as before.

sentences.zh: 令甘肅守臣徙其家屬京師。

translations.literal: The Gansu frontier officials were ordered to move his family to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in Gansu were ordered to relocate his household to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，忠之征沙漠也，獲番僧加失領真以獻。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong campaigned in the desert, he had captured the Tibetan monk Jia Shilingzhen and presented him as a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on Zhong's desert campaign, he had captured the Tibetan monk Jia Shilingzhen and sent him in tribute.

sentences.zh: 英宗赦不誅。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor pardoned him and did not execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong spared him and did not put him to death.

sentences.zh: 後逃之瓦剌，為也先用。

translations.literal: Later he fled to the Oirats and was employed by Esen.
translations.idiomatic: He later escaped to the Oirats and entered Esen's service.

sentences.zh: 憾忠，欲陷之。

translations.literal: Bearing a grudge against Zhong, he wished to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting Zhong, he sought to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 遂宣言忠與也先交通，而朝廷不察也。

translations.literal: He then spread word that Zhong was in contact with Esen, yet the court took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: He publicly claimed that Zhong was dealing with Esen, while the court failed to investigate.

sentences.zh: 英宗在塞外獨知之，比復辟，即召還。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor alone knew the truth while in captivity beyond the frontier; as soon as he was restored to the throne, he summoned Zhong back.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong alone knew this while held on the northern frontier; once restored, he immediately recalled Zhong.

sentences.zh: 而忠在福建亦屢有斬馘功，乃擢都督同知，充左副總兵，鎮守甘肅。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Zhong, in Fujian, also won repeated victories of beheadings and captures; he was therefore promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, appointed left deputy commander-in-chief, and put in charge of defending Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong meanwhile scored repeated battlefield kills in Fujian, was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, made left deputy commander-in-chief, and stationed to defend Gansu.

sentences.zh: 陛見，慰諭甚至，賜玉帶、織金蟒衣。

translations.literal: On audience he was comforted and instructed at great length, and was granted a jade belt and a gold-brocade python robe.
translations.idiomatic: At court he received extensive reassurance and rewards, including a jade belt and a gold-embroidered python robe.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，寇大入甘肅，巡撫芮釗劾奏諸將失事罪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun, when bandits made a major incursion into Gansu, Grand Coordinator Rui Zhao memorialized charging the generals with failure.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 2, after a major raid into Gansu, Grand Coordinator Rui Zhao impeached the generals for their defeat.

sentences.zh: 部議忠功足贖罪，置不問。

translations.literal: The ministry ruled that Zhong's merit was sufficient to redeem his offense, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that Zhong's service outweighed his fault, and he was left unpunished.

sentences.zh: 三年以鎮番破賊功，進左都督。

translations.literal: In the third year, for merit in defeating the enemy at Zhenfan, he was advanced to left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, for crushing the enemy at Zhenfan, he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五年，孛來以數萬騎分掠西寧、莊浪、甘肅諸道，入涼州。
