translations.literal: In the fifth year, Bolai with tens of thousands of horsemen raided in separate columns along the routes of Xining, Zhuanglang, and Gansu, and entered Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Bolai led tens of thousands of cavalry in divided raids through Xining, Zhuanglang, and Gansu, penetrating as far as Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 忠鏖戰一日夜，矢盡力疲。

translations.literal: Zhong fought fiercely for a day and a night until his arrows were spent and his strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong battled for a full day and night until his arrows ran out and his men were spent.

sentences.zh: 賊來益眾，軍中皆失色。

translations.literal: The enemy grew ever more numerous, and everyone in the army turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy swelled in numbers, the troops lost heart.

sentences.zh: 忠意氣彌厲，拊循將士，復殊死鬥。

translations.literal: Zhong's spirit grew only fiercer; he rallied the officers and men and again fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's resolve hardened; he steadied his officers and soldiers and led another desperate stand.

sentences.zh: 賊見終不可勝，而援軍亦至，遂解去。

translations.literal: Seeing that they could not prevail after all, and that relief troops had also arrived, the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy saw they could not win and reinforcements appeared, they broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 忠竟全師還。

translations.literal: Zhong brought the whole army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong withdrew with his force intact.

sentences.zh: 七年，永昌、涼州、莊浪塞外諸番屢為邊患。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the various tribes beyond the passes of Yongchang, Liangzhou, and Zhuanglang repeatedly troubled the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, tribes beyond Yongchang, Liangzhou, and Zhuanglang repeatedly raided the border.

sentences.zh: 忠與總兵官衛穎分討之。

translations.literal: Zhong and the commander-in-chief Wei Ying divided forces to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Commander-in-Chief Wei Ying split up to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 忠先破巴哇諸大族。

translations.literal: Zhong first defeated the great Bawa clans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong first broke the major Bawa tribes.

sentences.zh: 其昝咂、馬吉思諸族，他將不能下者，忠復擊破之。

translations.literal: The Zanzha and Majisi clans, which other generals could not subdue, Zhong again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He also crushed the Zanzha and Majisi tribes, which other commanders had failed to bring down.

sentences.zh: 論功，忠止增祿百石，而穎乃得世券。

translations.literal: In the merit assessment, Zhong received only an increase of one hundred piculs of salary, whereas Wei Ying was granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: For merit, Zhong was given only an extra hundred piculs of grain salary, while Wei Ying received a hereditary noble patent.

sentences.zh: 忠以為言，遂封伏羌伯。

translations.literal: Zhong lodged a complaint about this, and was thereupon enfeoffed as Baron of Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong protested the disparity, and was then enfeoffed as Baron of Fuxiang.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，固原賊滿四據石城反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, the bandit Man Si seized Shicheng and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 4, the rebel Man Si held Shicheng and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 詔忠移師討之，與總督項忠等夾攻賊巢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhong to shift his army to suppress him; together with Grand Coordinator Xiang Zhong and others he attacked the rebel stronghold from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was ordered to move against him and, with Grand Coordinator Xiang Zhong and others, struck the rebel nest in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 忠由木頭溝直抵炮架山下，多所斬獲，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: Zhong advanced straight from Mutougou to the foot of Paojia Mountain, killing and capturing many; the rebels fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong marched from Mutougou straight to Paojia Mountain, inflicting heavy losses and forcing the rebels to give ground.

sentences.zh: 冒矢石連奪山北、山西兩峰，而項忠等軍亦克山之東峰。

translations.literal: Braving arrows and stones he seized in succession the northern and western peaks of the mountain, while Xiang Zhong's troops also took the eastern peak.
translations.idiomatic: Under heavy fire he took the mountain's north and west peaks in turn, while Xiang Zhong's force captured the east peak.

sentences.zh: 及石城東、西二門，賊大窘，相對哭。

translations.literal: When the eastern and western gates of Shicheng were reached, the rebels were in great distress and wept facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the east and west gates of Shicheng the rebels were trapped and wept across to one another.

sentences.zh: 忽昏霧起，他哨舉煙掣軍，賊遂並力攻忠。

translations.literal: Suddenly a thick mist arose; another detachment raised smoke and pulled back its troops, and the rebels then combined their strength to attack Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden fog descended; another column signaled with smoke and withdrew, and the rebels massed their full strength against Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠力戰不已，為流矢所中，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: Zhong fought on without cease and was struck by a stray arrow; he died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong kept fighting until a stray arrow struck him down; he was seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 從子海、孫鎧前救忠，亦死。

translations.literal: His nephew Hai and grandson Kai, who had rushed forward to rescue him, also died.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Hai and grandson Kai, who had gone ahead to save him, fell as well.

sentences.zh: 忠為將嚴紀律，善撫士。

translations.literal: As a commander Zhong enforced discipline strictly and was skilled at comforting his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was a strict disciplinarian and excelled at winning his soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，西陲人吊哭者相望於道。

translations.literal: At his death, mourners from the western marches lined the roads one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people of the western frontier mourned along the roads for miles.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈侯，謚武勇，予世券。

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis, given the posthumous title Wuyong, and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him a marquis with the temple name Wuyong and awarded a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，從有司言，建忠義坊於蘭州，以表其裏。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, on the recommendation of local officials, a Loyalty and Righteousness archway was erected at Lanzhou to honor his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, on local officials' petition, a Loyalty and Righteousness arch was raised at Lanzhou to mark his home district.

sentences.zh: 又從巡撫許進言，建武勇祠於甘州城東，春秋致祭。

translations.literal: Again, on Grand Coordinator Xu Jin's recommendation, a Wuyong shrine was built east of Ganzhou city, with sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Grand Coordinator Xu Jin's advice, a Wuyong shrine was founded east of Ganzhou, with rites each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 孫銳，襲伯爵。

translations.literal: His grandson Rui inherited the barony.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rui succeeded to the barony.

sentences.zh: 成化中，協守南京。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign he assisted in the defense of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua he helped defend Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，出鎮湖廣，改兩廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was sent to command Huguang, then was transferred to the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he took command in Huguang, then was moved to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 平蠻賊，累有功，鹹璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: He pacified Miao bandits with repeated merit and was repeatedly rewarded by imperial missives.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Miao rebels with repeated success and received repeated imperial commendations.

sentences.zh: 九年以廣西破賊，增歲祿二百石。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for defeating bandits in Guangxi, his annual salary was increased by two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, for victories in Guangxi, his yearly grain salary was raised by two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 言官劾銳廣置邸舍，私造大舶以通番商。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Rui for widely establishing lodges and privately building large ships to trade with foreign merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists charged Rui with maintaining many town houses and building large vessels on his own to trade with overseas merchants.

sentences.zh: 置不問。

translations.literal: No action was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action.

sentences.zh: 思恩土官岑浚反，與總督潘蕃討平之。

translations.literal: When the native official of Sien, Cen Jun, rebelled, Rui joined Grand Coordinator Pan Fan in suppressing and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sien native official Cen Jun rose in revolt, Rui and Grand Coordinator Pan Fan campaigned and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 既又討平賀縣僮賊。

translations.literal: He then also campaigned and pacified the Zhuang bandits of He County.
translations.idiomatic: He next suppressed the Zhuang rebels of He County as well.

sentences.zh: 加官至太子太傅。

translations.literal: His office was raised to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，劉瑾欲殺尚書劉大夏，坐以處置田州事失宜，並逮銳下詔獄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, Liu Jin wished to kill Minister Liu Daxia; citing mishandling of the Tianzhou affair, he had Liu Daxia and Rui seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 3, Liu Jin sought to destroy Minister Liu Daxia; charging mishandling of the Tianzhou campaign, he had Liu Daxia and Rui thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 獄具，革其加官並歲祿五百石。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Rui's added rank and five hundred piculs of annual salary were stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: After judgment, his honorary rank and an added five hundred piculs of salary were revoked.

sentences.zh: 已而賄瑾，起督漕運。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he bribed Jin and was reappointed to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He soon bribed Jin and was restored to command of the grain-transport service.

sentences.zh: 逾年，瑾誅，被劾罷。

translations.literal: The next year, after Jin was executed, he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when Jin was put to death, he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 六年，盜劉宸等擾畿甸，命銳與中官谷大用討之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the bandits Liu Chen and others ravaged the capital region, Rui was ordered to campaign against them together with the eunuch Gu Dayong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, as Liu Chen's bandits harried the metropolitan districts, Rui was ordered to suppress them with the eunuch Gu Dayong.

sentences.zh: 所統京軍皆驕惰不習戰。

translations.literal: The capital troops under his command were all arrogant, lazy, and unaccustomed to fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan army he led was spoiled, idle, and unused to battle.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，遇賊於長垣，與戰大敗，身被傷，亡將印。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he met the bandits at Changyuan; he was badly defeated in battle, was himself wounded, and lost his commander's seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he engaged the rebels at Changyuan, suffered a crushing defeat, was wounded, and lost his general's seal.

sentences.zh: 會許泰援軍至，僅免。

translations.literal: When Xu Tai's relief army arrived, he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Relief under Xu Tai arrived just in time to save him.

sentences.zh: 言官交劾，乃召還。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached him in succession, and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: A stream of memorialists attacked him, and he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 以與大用同事，竟不罪。

translations.literal: Because he had served together with Dayong, in the end he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: As he had shared command with Dayong, he was not punished after all.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，復起鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, Rui was again appointed to command Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiajing accession he was again posted to command Huguang.

sentences.zh: 居三年卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after three years in post.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚威襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Weixiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the temple name Weixiang.

sentences.zh: 傳子江及漢。

translations.literal: The title passed to his sons Jiang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to his sons Jiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 漢，嘉靖中掌南京左府，提督操江，改總督漕運。

translations.literal: Han, in the Jiajing reign, held the left office of the Nanjing military commission, supervised training on the Yangzi, and was later made overall supervisor of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Han, under Jiajing, headed the left bureau of the Nanjing military commission, directed Yangzi River training, and was later appointed to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 未上，給事中楊上林劾其所至貪墨，詔褫職逮問。

translations.literal: Before he took up the grain-transport post, the supervising secretary Yang Shanglin impeached him for corruption wherever he had served; an edict stripped his office and ordered his arrest for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed the transport post, Supervising Secretary Yang Shanglin charged him with graft at every post; an edict removed him and ordered him seized for investigation.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，從子桓嗣。

translations.literal: He died without sons, and his nephew Huan succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died childless, and his nephew Huan inherited the peerage.

sentences.zh: 卒，子登嗣。

translations.literal: When Huan died, his son Deng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Deng succeeded after him.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，掌中軍府事垂二十年。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, Deng presided over the central military commission for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, Deng directed the central military commission for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 又再傳而明亡。

translations.literal: After two more generations the dynasty fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 成化初，趙輔、韓雍征大藤峽賊，詔勇以所部從征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, when Zhao Fu and Han Yong campaigned against the bandits of Dateng Gorge, an edict ordered Yong to join the expedition with his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, as Zhao Fu and Han Yong campaigned against the Dateng Gorge rebels, Yong was ordered to take his troops on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 其冬，賊大破，進左都督，增祿百石。

translations.literal: That winter the bandits were thoroughly broken; he was advanced to left commissioner-in-chief and his salary increased by one hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels were crushed; he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief with an added hundred piculs of salary.

sentences.zh: 三年召督效勇營訓練。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned to supervise training in the Valiant Service Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was recalled to drill the Valiant Service Camp.

sentences.zh: 尋上言：「大藤峽之役，臣與趙輔同功。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "In the Dateng Gorge campaign I shared merit with Zhao Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted: "In the Dateng Gorge campaign Zhao Fu and I won equal merit.

sentences.zh: 輔還京，余賊復叛。

translations.literal: Fu returned to the capital, and the remaining bandits rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Fu returned to court while the remnant rebels rose again.

sentences.zh: 臣親搗賊巢，縶其魁，誅其黨，還被掠男女四千人。

translations.literal: I personally stormed their nest, bound their chieftain, executed their partisans, and recovered four thousand men and women who had been carried off.
translations.idiomatic: I myself smashed their stronghold, seized their leader, killed their followers, and recovered four thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 今輔已封伯，而臣止進秩，惟陛下憐察。

translations.literal: Now Fu has been enfeoffed as a baron, while I have received only a promotion in rank; I beg Your Majesty to take pity and look into this."
translations.idiomatic: Fu has been made a baron, yet I have only been promoted in rank; I beg Your Majesty to consider this fairly."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗以勇再著戰功，特封靖安伯。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor, because Yong had again distinguished himself in battle, specially enfeoffed him as Baron of Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong, noting Yong's fresh battlefield merit, specially enfeoffed him as Baron of Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 十年卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 10.

sentences.zh: 謚武敏，世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wumin, with hereditary succession as commander.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wumin, with hereditary succession as commander.

sentences.zh: 勇性廉謹。

translations.literal: Yong was by nature frugal and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was frugal and discreet by nature.

sentences.zh: 在兩廣時，諸將多營私漁利，勇獨無所取。

translations.literal: While in the Two Guangs, most generals enriched themselves by private dealings, but Yong took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Guangs most commanders lined their pockets, yet Yong took no private gain.

sentences.zh: 時論稱之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 羅秉忠，初名克羅俄領占，沙州衛都督僉事困即來子也。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhong, originally named Kelaoe Lingzhan, was the son of Kunjilai, assistant commissioner of the Shazhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhong, born Kelaoe Lingzhan, was son of Kunjilai, assistant commissioner of the Shazhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 兄喃哥既襲父職，英宗復命秉忠為指揮使，協理衛事。

translations.literal: After his elder brother Nange had inherited their father's post, the Yingzong Emperor also appointed Bingzhong commander to assist in administering the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once his brother Nange succeeded to their father's office, Yingzong also named Bingzhong commander to help run the guard.

sentences.zh: 既而喃哥率千二百人內徙，詔居之東昌、平山二衛，給田廬什器，所以撫恤甚厚。

translations.literal: Later Nange led twelve hundred people in moving inward; an edict settled them in the Dongchang and Pingshan guards, granting fields, houses, and utensils—the favors of support were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Later Nange led twelve hundred people to resettle inside the border; they were placed in the Dongchang and Pingshan guards with land, housing, and goods, and were treated with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 喃哥卒，秉忠為都指揮使，代領其眾。

translations.literal: When Nange died, Bingzhong became commander and took over his following.
translations.idiomatic: After Nange's death, Bingzhong became commander and led his people.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，塞上多警。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor was taken north, alarms multiplied along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong's capture on the northern campaign, the frontier was rife with alarms.

sentences.zh: 朝議恐降人乘機為變，欲徙之南方。

translations.literal: Court discussion feared that surrendered peoples might seize the moment to rebel and wished to move them south.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared the resettled tribes might exploit the crisis and debated relocating them south.

sentences.zh: 會貴州苗亂，都督毛福壽南征，即擢秉忠都督僉事，率所部援剿。

translations.literal: Just then the Miao of Guizhou rose; Commissioner Mao Shou led a southern campaign, and Bingzhong was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief and ordered to lead his men in support.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guizhou Miao rebelled, Commissioner Mao Shou marched south; Bingzhong was raised to assistant commissioner-in-chief and sent with his troops to assist.

sentences.zh: 積戰功至左都督。

translations.literal: Through accumulated battle merit he reached left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by repeated victories to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天順初，始賜姓名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was first granted his Chinese name.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun he first received his formal Chinese name.

sentences.zh: 曹欽之反，番官多從之者。

translations.literal: When Cao Qin rebelled, many of the frontier officers followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In Cao Qin's revolt many frontier officers joined him.

sentences.zh: 秉忠亦坐下獄，籍其家。

translations.literal: Bingzhong was also imprisoned and his household property was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong too was thrown into prison and his family property was seized.

sentences.zh: 久之，上章自辯，乃得釋。

translations.literal: After a long time he submitted a memorial in his own defense and was released.
translations.idiomatic: After long imprisonment he memorialized in self-defense and was freed.

sentences.zh: 成化初，尚書程信討山都掌蠻，秉忠以遊擊將軍從。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, when Minister Cheng Xin campaigned against the Shanduzhang Miao, Bingzhong followed as a mobile-column general.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, when Minister Cheng Xin attacked the Shanduzhang Miao, Bingzhong served as mobile-column general under him.

sentences.zh: 既抵永寧，分兵六道。

translations.literal: After reaching Yongning, the army divided into six routes.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yongning the force split into six columns.

sentences.zh: 秉忠由金鵝江進，大破之。

translations.literal: Bingzhong advanced by the Jine River and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong marched up the Jine River and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 論功，封順義伯。

translations.literal: When his merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 十六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 謚榮壯，子孫世指揮使。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Rongzhuang; his descendants held the hereditary rank of commander in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Rongzhuang, and his descendants held the hereditary rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明興，諸番部懷太祖功德，多樂內附，賜姓名授官職者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the founding of Ming, the various tribal departments, cherishing the founding emperor's merit and virtue, mostly rejoiced in attaching themselves within the empire; those granted surnames and appointed to office cannot be fully reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: At the founding of Ming, the various tribal departments, cherishing the founding emperor's merit and virtue, mostly rejoiced in submitting to the empire; those granted surnames and appointed to office are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 繼以成祖銳意遠圖，震耀威武，於是吳允誠、金忠之徒，率眾來屬，遂得列爵授任，比肩勛舊。

translations.literal: Subsequently Emperor Chengzu keenly pursued far-reaching plans and displayed awe-inspiring might, so men such as Wu Yuncheng and Jin Zhong led their followers to submit and were then able to receive ranks and appointments on a par with the meritorious veterans.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Chengzu, intent on far-reaching designs and displaying awe-inspiring might, drew men such as Wu Yuncheng and Jin Zhong to lead their followers in submission; they received ranks and appointments alongside the old merit holders.

sentences.zh: 或以戰功自奮，錫券受封，傳世不絕。

translations.literal: Some through military achievement exerted themselves, received patents of investiture, and transmitted their titles without end.
translations.idiomatic: Others rose through military achievement, received investiture patents, and passed their titles down for generations.

sentences.zh: 視夫陸梁倔強者，順逆殊異，不其昭歟！

translations.literal: Compared with those who were violent and stubborn, the difference between compliance and resistance is quite clear, is it not!
translations.idiomatic: Compared with those who were violent and defiant, how clear is the contrast between submission and resistance!

sentences.zh: 土木以還，勢以不競，邊政日弛，火篩、俺答諸部騷動無寧歲。

translations.literal: From the Tumu crisis onward strength could not contend; frontier governance daily grew lax, and the Huosha, Anda, and other tribes stirred unrest year after year without a peaceful one.
translations.idiomatic: After Tumu the dynasty could no longer compete; frontier governance slackened daily, and the Huosha, Anda, and other tribes stirred trouble almost every year.

sentences.zh: 盛衰之故概可考焉。

translations.literal: The causes of rise and decline may in the main be examined here.
translations.idiomatic: The broad pattern of rise and decline may be traced here.
